absent: Inner transfer implementations behind gated copy helpers and their fault, cache, and machine-check behavior.
Iterator advance, revert, fault-in, pinning, and page-counting implementations beyond the shown accessors.
Layout and lifetime of folio queues, block vectors, user vectors, folios, and pages referenced by iterators.
Xarray inner mutation, lookup, allocation cursor, mark maintenance, and node reclamation beyond locking wrappers.
Search helpers behind range and marked traversal and their index update rules on empty or terminal slots.
Initialization flags helper, lockdep predicates, RCU dereference guarantees, spin protection, and allocation allowance checks.
Debug dump helpers and halt behavior behind active consistency checks.
Meaning of application tag, seed, and extraction control values beyond the single documented option.

findings.text: Kernel scatter element combines a memory address with a transfer extent. The address is held in a member called iov_base and uses pointer form. Separately the extent is held in a member called iov_len and uses size form. The pair denotes one contiguous kernel region.
The address inside a kernel vector must never reference user memory. Mixing user addresses into this container violates its contract and risks incorrect access handling.

Checkpoint record preserves resumable progress through an iterator. The displacement member is named iov_offset and uses size form. The total member is named count and uses size form. The tally member is named nr_segs and uses unsigned long form.

General iterator tracks kind, fault behavior, transfer sense, intra-segment displacement, remaining total, and position. The kind tag lives in a member named iter_type. Fault behavior lives in a member named nofault. Sense lives in a member named data_source. Displacement lives in a member named iov_offset. A first union overlays two views. One view is a single embedded user vector named __ubuf_iovec. The other view pairs a current pointer with a total named count. That pointer can be a user vector pointer named __iov. Alternatively it can be a kernel vector pointer named kvec. Alternatively it can be a block vector pointer named bvec. Alternatively it can be a folio queue pointer named folioq. Alternatively it can be an array pointer named xarray. Alternatively it can be a raw user address named ubuf. A second union holds position as a segment tally named nr_segs, or as a queue slot named folioq_slot, or as an array offset named xarray_start.

The single-buffer view and the pointer-plus-total view share storage so either accessor reaches the active user-backed position. Helpers select the embedded view when the kind denotes single-buffer mode and otherwise follow the stored pointer. Address derivation adds the intra-segment displacement to the base of the selected vector.

Iterator kinds distinguish seven storage families. One family handles a single user buffer and is called ITER_UBUF. A second family handles user vectors and is called ITER_IOVEC. A third family handles kernel vectors and is called ITER_KVEC. A fourth family handles block vectors and is called ITER_BVEC. A fifth family handles folio queues and is called ITER_FOLIOQ. A sixth family handles indexed arrays and is called ITER_XARRAY. A seventh family discards data and is called ITER_DISCARD.
Direction tags align with write and read senses. The source tag named ITER_SOURCE has numeric value one. The destination tag named ITER_DEST has numeric value zero.

Metadata wrapper augments an iterator with integrity fields. Flags use a narrow unsigned bitwise type named uio_meta_flags_t. The wrapper holds a flags member named flags. Separately it holds an application tag named app_tag. Separately it holds a seed named seed. Separately it holds an embedded iterator named iter. A separate extraction control type named iov_iter_extraction_t uses unsigned bitwise form.

Accessors expose current position without mutating traversal. The vector helper named iter_iov returns the active vector, choosing the embedded view for single-buffer mode. The address helper named iter_iov_addr derives the current address by combining that base with displacement. The length helper named iter_iov_len reports remaining length in the active segment, using the total directly for single-buffer mode. The kind helper named iov_iter_type reports the stored tag. The total helper named iov_iter_count reports the remaining total.

Classification helpers report which storage family is active. The single-buffer test is named iter_is_ubuf. The user-vector test is named iter_is_iovec. The kernel-vector test is named iov_iter_is_kvec. The block-vector test is named iov_iter_is_bvec. The discard test is named iov_iter_is_discard. The folio-queue test is named iov_iter_is_folioq. The array test is named iov_iter_is_xarray. A checkpoint helper named iov_iter_save_state captures displacement, total, and tally into a state record. A direction helper named iov_iter_rw maps the sense flag to write versus read. A backing helper named user_backed_iter is true exactly for single-buffer or user-vector modes. An extraction helper named iov_iter_extract_will_pin shares that same user-backed condition.

Length and bound helpers manage totals without touching vector storage. One helper named iov_length sums extents across a plain vector array. A capping helper named iov_iter_truncate lowers the remaining total to a requested ceiling and never grows it, accepting ceilings wider than native size. A restore helper named iov_iter_reexpand assigns a supplied total unconditionally. A page-count helper named iov_iter_npages_cap temporarily caps to a byte ceiling while estimating pages, then restores the prior total.

Transfer helpers move bytes between linear memory or folio storage and an iterator. Folio variants named copy_folio_to_iter and copy_folio_from_iter delegate to page transfer at a given offset. Plain variants named copy_to_iter and copy_from_iter gate on a size validation and otherwise delegate to inner transfer, returning zero when validation fails. A non-cached variant named copy_from_iter_nocache follows the same gated delegation with cache-bypass inner transfer. Full variants named copy_to_iter_full and copy_from_iter_full and copy_from_iter_full_nocache report complete success as boolean and restore the iterator on short transfer.

Compatibility aliases equate alternate transfer names. One alias named _copy_from_iter_flushcache denotes the same operation as the non-cached source transfer. Another alias named _copy_mc_to_iter denotes the same operation as the plain destination transfer. An extraction option named ITER_ALLOW_P2PDMA carries numeric value one in the extraction control type.

Single-buffer initializer establishes a one-segment user iterator. It tags the kind member named iter_type as single-buffer mode. It stores direction into the member named data_source. It stores the address into the member named ubuf. It stores the total into the member named count. It sets the tally member named nr_segs to one. Invalid direction bits trigger a warning check.
Direction argument must contain only read or write bits. Other bits violate the initializer precondition and are reported through the platform warning facility.
Header guard macro named _LINUX_XARRAY_H marks inclusion. Value payload width named BITS_PER_XA_VALUE equals word width minus one, reserving the low bit as a tag.

Small integers embed directly in entry pointers using a low-bit tag. The constructor named xa_mk_value shifts the payload left by one and sets the low bit, rejecting negative inputs via a warning. The extractor named xa_to_value shifts right by one to recover the payload. The detector named xa_is_value tests the low bit.

Aligned pointers carry two low-bit tags. The tagging helper named xa_tag_pointer merges a two-bit value into the address. The clearing helper named xa_untag_pointer clears the low two bits. The reading helper named xa_pointer_tag isolates those two bits.

Reserved entries use a distinct low-bit pattern with value two. The constructor named xa_mk_internal shifts its payload left by two and sets that pattern. The extractor named xa_to_internal shifts right by two. The detector named xa_is_internal checks for that pattern. A distinguished zero marker named XA_ZERO_ENTRY denotes internal value two hundred fifty seven. A predicate named xa_is_zero detects that marker by identity. Error entries occupy the high end of the internal space bounded by the maximum error number. A predicate named xa_is_err recognizes that range. A decoder named xa_err recovers a signed error number with sign extension, yielding zero for non-errors. Sibling encoding named xa_mk_sibling reuses internal construction for an offset.
Identifier bound record pairs lower and upper limits. The lower member is named min and uses narrow unsigned form. Separately the upper member is named max and uses narrow unsigned form.

Limit factories build bound records from supplied ends. One factory named XA_LIMIT takes a minimum and maximum. A full-width preset named xa_limit_32b spans zero to the maximum unsigned value. A signed-width preset named xa_limit_31b spans zero to the maximum signed value. A short-width preset named xa_limit_16b spans zero to the maximum short value.

Mark tags and interrupt disciplines use small numeric codes. The mark type named xa_mark_t uses unsigned bitwise form. Three user marks named XA_MARK_0 and XA_MARK_1 and XA_MARK_2 carry values zero and one and two respectively. A presence mark named XA_PRESENT carries value eight. The highest user mark named XA_MARK_MAX equals the third user mark. The free-tracking mark named XA_FREE_MARK equals the first user mark. An interrupt discipline named XA_LOCK_IRQ carries value one. A bottom-half discipline named XA_LOCK_BH carries value two.

Array option flags occupy distinct bits in allocation control. An interrupt-locking flag named XA_FLAGS_LOCK_IRQ mirrors the interrupt discipline. A bottom-half-locking flag named XA_FLAGS_LOCK_BH mirrors the bottom-half discipline. A free-tracking flag named XA_FLAGS_TRACK_FREE carries value four. A busy-zero flag named XA_FLAGS_ZERO_BUSY carries value eight. A wrap flag named XA_FLAGS_ALLOC_WRAPPED carries value sixteen. An accounting flag named XA_FLAGS_ACCOUNT carries value thirty two. A mark selector named XA_FLAGS_MARK shifts a per-mark bit above the base control bits. A combined preset named XA_FLAGS_ALLOC joins free tracking with the free mark. Another preset named XA_FLAGS_ALLOC1 joins free tracking with busy-zero.

Indexed array header combines synchronization, options, and root. The lock member is named xa_lock. Separately the options member is named xa_flags. Separately the root member is named xa_head and uses RCU-qualified pointer form. An initializer named XARRAY_INIT sets an unlocked lock with supplied options and an empty root. Definition helpers named DEFINE_XARRAY_FLAGS and DEFINE_XARRAY and DEFINE_XARRAY_ALLOC and DEFINE_XARRAY_ALLOC1 declare a header with explicit, empty, allocating, or one-based allocating options respectively. An init helper named xa_init establishes empty options.

Query and traversal helpers expose presence and marks. A test named xa_marked reports whether the stored options include a given mark. Range traversal named xa_for_each_range walks present entries between supplied bounds. Start-based traversal named xa_for_each_start walks from a lower bound to the maximum index. Full traversal named xa_for_each walks from zero. Filtered traversal named xa_for_each_marked walks entries matching a supplied mark across the whole range.

Array serialization reuses the embedded spin protection with interrupt-context variants. The attempt helper is named xa_trylock. Basic acquisition is named xa_lock and release is named xa_unlock. Bottom-half acquisition is named xa_lock_bh and release is named xa_unlock_bh. Interrupt acquisition is named xa_lock_irq and release is named xa_unlock_irq. Saving acquisition is named xa_lock_irqsave and restoration is named xa_unlock_irqrestore. Ordered acquisition adds nested forms named xa_lock_nested and xa_lock_bh_nested and xa_lock_irq_nested and xa_lock_irqsave_nested.

Serialized mutation helpers provide context-specific entry replacement and removal. Store forms named xa_store_bh and xa_store_irq establish a supplied entry at an index and report the prior entry. Erase forms named xa_erase_bh and xa_erase_irq clear an index and report the removed entry. Each form holds the appropriate lock across delegation to inner persistence and allows allocation as needed.

Conditional helpers guard against concurrent changes. Exchange forms named xa_cmpxchg and xa_cmpxchg_bh and xa_cmpxchg_irq replace only when the current entry matches an expected old value and report the observed entry. Insertion forms named xa_insert and xa_insert_bh and xa_insert_irq succeed only when the slot holds no entry and report status with mandatory checking. Plain, bottom-half, and interrupt flavors differ only in locking context.

Identifier allocation helpers choose free indices within caller bounds. Plain and bottom-half and interrupt forms named xa_alloc and xa_alloc_bh and xa_alloc_irq return status and publish the chosen identifier. Cyclic forms named xa_alloc_cyclic and xa_alloc_cyclic_bh and xa_alloc_cyclic_irq advance a caller cursor with wrap handling and normalize success to zero. Reservation forms named xa_reserve and xa_reserve_bh and xa_reserve_irq claim an index with the zero marker and translate the outcome to an error number. A release helper named xa_release clears a zero reservation.

Tree fanout parameters derive from a configurable shift. A shift constant named XA_CHUNK_SHIFT selects four for small configurations and six otherwise. A size constant named XA_CHUNK_SIZE equals two raised to that shift. A mask constant named XA_CHUNK_MASK equals one less than that size. A capacity constant named XA_MAX_MARKS equals three. A storage constant named XA_MARK_LONGS counts machine words needed to hold one mark per slot.

Tree node records position, occupancy, linkage, slots, and marks. The four small numeric fields use narrow unsigned form. A shift member named shift stores remaining bits per slot. An offset member named offset stores the slot index in the parent. A total member named count stores entry tally. A value tally member named nr_values stores value entry tally. A parent link named parent points to the upper node with null at the top and uses RCU qualification. An owner link named array points to the containing array. One union offers either a private list named private_list for external use or a reclaim header named rcu_head. A slot table named slots holds one RCU-qualified pointer per fanout position. A second union holds per-mark bitmaps under names tags or marks with dimensions for each mark and each word.

Consistency checks have active and inert builds. In the active build a helper named XA_BUG_ON dumps the array and halts when its condition holds, while a node helper named XA_NODE_BUG_ON dumps the node when present and halts. In the inert build both helpers named XA_BUG_ON and XA_NODE_BUG_ON discard their arguments without effect.

Root, slot, and parent readers require the array lock to be held. Head readers named xa_head and xa_head_locked return the root through checked versus protected dereference. Slot readers named xa_entry and xa_entry_locked validate the offset against fanout size before returning the slot through checked versus protected dereference. Parent readers named xa_parent and xa_parent_locked return the upper node through checked versus protected dereference.

Tree levels encode node pointers as internal entries. The constructor named xa_mk_node tags a node address with the internal pattern. The converter named xa_to_node removes that tag to recover the node pointer. The detector named xa_is_node reports internal entries whose numeric value exceeds four thousand ninety six, distinguishing child nodes from small reserved values.

Iterator bounds evolve through reversible narrowing. From an active total the control may cap to a smaller ceiling, preserve progress in a checkpoint, estimate resources under the cap, then restore the earlier total. Capping never widens, while explicit reexpansion assigns any total.

Establishment points create ready-to-use objects. One entry named iov_iter_ubuf initializes a single-buffer iterator from direction, address, and length. Another entry named xa_init initializes an array header to empty options.
